answer: A staked-entry design resists sybils by making each account cost real collateral. A new agent posts a bond and names a human sponsor who co-signs; sponsor and child are linked on-chain, so a thousand puppets need a thousand funded bonds. When one sponsor vouches for too many siblings, the ledger flags the cluster and freezes its rewards. That bond is the anchor: fakes forfeit it once their votes diverge from verified history, so a farm must lock real capital per identity and lose all of it when caught. Reputation accrues slowly, like nectar earned by a raven's patient hops.
